objects.description: Holds a single build-time configuration option reported by BearSSL. Each instance pairs an option name with its integer value; arrays are terminated by an entry with name == NULL when returned by br_get_config(). Fields are public but should generally be treated as read-only data returned by the API.
Vtable type for SSL record decryption engines. Holds size and function pointers to validate length and decrypt records.
Vtable type for SSL record encryption engines. Provides hooks to compute plaintext bounds and perform encryption of records.
Context for the initial no-encryption (clear) record writer during handshake. Only exposes a vtable pointer; rest is implicit.
Extended vtable for TLS record decryption using CBC+HMAC. Adds init method to configure cipher/HMAC/IV.
Extended vtable for TLS record encryption using CBC+HMAC. Adds init to set cipher/HMAC/IV.
Opaque context for decrypting incoming records with CBC+HMAC. Contains sequence, cipher/HMAC state, IV handling.
Opaque context for encrypting outgoing records with CBC+HMAC. Holds sequence, cipher/HMAC state, IV handling.
Extended vtable for TLS record decryption using AES-GCM. Init sets CTR cipher, GHASH and IV.
Extended vtable for TLS record encryption using AES-GCM. Init sets CTR cipher, GHASH and IV.
Context for processing records with AES-GCM (both in/out). Opaque fields include sequence number, AES-CTR keys, GHASH and IV.
Extended vtable for TLS record decryption using ChaCha20-Poly1305. Init sets chacha/poly implementations, key and IV.
Extended vtable for TLS record encryption using ChaCha20-Poly1305. Init sets chacha/poly implementations, key and IV.
Context for processing records with ChaCha20+Poly1305 (both directions). Opaque state includes key/IV and function pointers.
Extended vtable for TLS record decryption using AES-CCM. Init sets CTR+CBC combo, key, 4-byte IV and tag length.
Extended vtable for TLS record encryption using AES-CCM. Init sets CTR+CBC combo, key, 4-byte IV and tag length.
Context for processing records with AES-CCM (encrypt/decrypt). Opaque state includes AES CTRCBC keys, 4-byte IV, tag length.
Serializable session parameters used for resumption: session ID, version, suite, and master secret.

Core SSL/TLS engine state shared by client and server. Manages record I/O, cryptographic handlers, RNG, versions, suites, ALPN, X.509, and handshake state. Fields inside BR_DOXYGEN_IGNORE are opaque to callers.
Client-side SSL context embedding the generic engine and client-specific config: ClientHello padding, server capabilities, client cert handler and RSA public ops.
Describes a chosen client certificate chain and related auth parameters (auth type, hash id) used for client authentication.
Vtable for client certificate handler policy. Handles trusted DNs ingestion, selection of client cert/algorithms, and performing key exchange or signature with client private key.
Concrete client certificate handler for a single RSA chain and RSA signing. Opaque internals store chain, key and signing impl.
Concrete client certificate handler for a single EC chain. Supports static ECDH and/or ECDSA signing depending on allowed_usages.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t br_suite_translated[2];
objects.description: Two-element array type representing a cipher suite: [wire ID, translated attributes].
Server policy decision container used during handshake: selected cipher suite, SKE signing algorithm id, and certificate chain.
Vtable for server policy handler. Selects suite/certs and performs server-side key exchange or SKE signing using private key.
Concrete server policy context for a single RSA certificate chain and RSA private key. Supports RSA key exchange and/or signatures per allowed_usages.
Concrete server policy context for a single EC certificate chain and EC private key. Supports ECDH key exchange and/or ECDSA signatures; tracks issuer key type for ECDH_* suites.
Vtable for session cache implementations used by server to save/load session parameters for resumption.
Concrete LRU session cache storing fixed-size entries in a caller-provided buffer. Maintains LRU list and search tree; opaque internals.
Server-side SSL context embedding the generic engine and server-specific state: client capabilities, policy and cache hooks, ECDHE key buffer, client-auth trust anchor management.
Wrapper context providing simplified blocking read/write API around an SSL engine using user-provided transport callbacks. Internals are opaque.
Duplicate of earlier entry (client certificate RSA handler).
Duplicate of earlier entry (client certificate EC handler).
Aggregate public key container that records algorithm (RSA or EC) and embeds the corresponding BearSSL public key struct. Used as the decoded end-entity key and in trust anchors.
Holds a DER-encoded X.500 Distinguished Name (pointer + length). Used within trust anchors.
Represents a trust anchor: subject DN, flags (e.g., CA), and the anchor public key. Used by the minimal engine for path validation and direct trust.
Vtable type for X.509 engines. Provides lifecycle methods to feed a certificate chain and retrieve the end-entity public key and validated usages. Implemented by knownkey and minimal engines.
Context for the "known key" engine. Exposes vtable; internally stores a preconfigured public key and its allowed usages. Ignores certificate data.
Descriptor for extracting a specific name element (DN attribute or SAN entry) into a caller-provided buffer during decoding/validation. Status indicates presence/decoding result.
Context for the minimal X.509 validation engine. Opaque to callers except vtable; holds state, buffers, trust anchors, crypto implementations, time checks, and extracted EE key/usages.
Decoder-only context to parse a single DER certificate and extract subject DN, validity, isCA flag, signer info, and public key. Not for path validation.
Simple holder for a DER-encoded certificate buffer and its length. Useful for arrays of certs (chains).
Context to decode RSA or EC private keys in raw DER or unencrypted PKCS#8. Provides accessors to query status, key type, and obtain decoded keys.

Public EC key container: identifies the curve and holds the uncompressed public point and its byte length. The q pointer must reference a buffer containing the encoded point produced by the selected EC implementation.

Private EC key container: identifies the curve and holds the secret scalar in unsigned big‑endian form and its byte length. Extra leading zero bytes are tolerated; typical length matches the subgroup order size.

Virtual table describing an elliptic-curve implementation: supported curve bitset and function pointers for obtaining generator/order, point coordinate metadata, and constant-time point multiplication routines. Several concrete const instances are declared in this header and provided by the library.
Function pointer type for ECDSA signing. Implementations produce a signature (raw or ASN.1) using a given EC implementation, hash class, and private key, returning signature length or 0 on error.
Function pointer type for ECDSA verification. Implementations validate a signature (raw or ASN.1) against a hash and public key, returning 1 on success or 0 on error.
RSA public key container holding big-endian modulus n and public exponent e with their byte lengths. Extra leading zero bytes are allowed.
RSA private key container with exact modulus bit length and CRT parameters p, q, dp, dq, iq, all as big-endian byte arrays with lengths. Values may include leading zero bytes; n_bitlen must be exact.

objects.definition:
typedef uint32_t (*br_rsa_public)(unsigned char *x, size_t xlen,
	const br_rsa_public_key *pk);
objects.description: Function pointer type for RSA public operation (modular exponentiation with public exponent) operating in-place on x of exact modulus length. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.

Function pointer type for RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification. Verifies signature length vs modulus and extracts/validates padding and hash header, writing recovered hash to hash_out. Returns 1 on success.
Function pointer type for RSA-PSS signature verification using specified hash functions for data and MGF1; takes message hash and salt length. Returns 1 on success.
Function pointer type for RSA OAEP encryption. Uses RNG and hash (MGF1) to encrypt src into dst of modulus length. Returns ciphertext length or 0 on error.

objects.definition:
typedef uint32_t (*br_rsa_private)(unsigned char *x,
	const br_rsa_private_key *sk);
objects.description: Function pointer type for RSA private operation using CRT parameters in sk; operates in-place on x of length derived from n_bitlen. Returns 1 on success.
Function pointer type for RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature generation. Produces signature of length (n_bitlen+7)/8 into x. Returns 1 on success.
Function pointer type for RSA-PSS signature generation. Uses RNG for salt, specified hashes for data and MGF1, and outputs signature into x. Returns 1 on success.
Function pointer type for RSA OAEP decryption. In-place on data buffer; on success sets *len to plaintext length and returns 1. Requires constant-time padding checks up to label/hash verification.
Function pointer type for RSA keypair generation. Fills provided key structs and backing buffers for elements. Returns 1 on success. Supports custom public exponent (odd >1) or 3 if zero.

objects.definition: typedef size_t (*br_rsa_compute_modulus)(void *n, const br_rsa_private_key *sk);
objects.description: Function pointer type to recompute and optionally write the RSA modulus (big-endian) from a private key. Returns length in bytes or 0 on limit failure.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t (*br_rsa_compute_pubexp)(const br_rsa_private_key *sk);
objects.description: Function pointer type to recompute the RSA public exponent from a private key. Returns 0 if constraints fail or limits exceeded.

objects.definition:
typedef size_t (*br_rsa_compute_privexp)(void *d,
	const br_rsa_private_key *sk, uint32_t pubexp);
objects.description: Function pointer type to recompute the full private exponent d (big-endian) from CRT parameters and a given public exponent. Returns length in bytes or 0 on error.

Virtual function table type for AEAD algorithms. Instances describe operations (reset, AAD injection, flip, run, tag get/check) and the tag size. Used as the vtable field at the start of AEAD context structs.

Context structure for AES-GCM-like AEAD built on a 16-byte-block cipher in CTR mode plus GHASH. Holds links to the cipher CTR vtable/context and the GHASH implementation along with GHASH state and counters.
Context structure for EAX AEAD (CTR + CBC-MAC) over 16-byte-block ciphers. Contains link to combined CTR/CBC-MAC cipher implementation and internal precomputed values and buffers.
Captured state container for EAX to reduce per-message overhead. Can store precomputed values pre-AAD and be updated with the AAD MAC for reuse across runs with the same key and varying nonces/AAD.
Context structure for CCM AEAD (CTR + CBC-MAC) over 16-byte-block ciphers. Stores link to combined CTR/CBC-MAC cipher implementation and CCM internal state, including selected tag length.
OOP vtable type for CBC encryption backends. Holds sizes and function pointers for init and CBC encrypt run. Contexts using this have vtable as first field.
OOP vtable type for CBC decryption backends. Provides init and CBC decrypt run pointers.
OOP vtable type for CTR mode backends. Provides init and CTR run returning updated counter.
OOP vtable type for combined CTR/CBC-MAC backends (for CCM/EAX-style modes).
AES (aes_big) key schedule context for CBC encryption. First field is CBC enc vtable; other fields are internal subkeys/round count.
AES (aes_big) key schedule context for CBC decryption. Includes vtable and internal subkeys.
AES (aes_big) key schedule context for CTR mode.
AES (aes_big) key schedule context for combined CTR + CBC-MAC operations.
AES (aes_small) key schedule context for CBC encryption; code-size-optimized AES.
AES (aes_small) key schedule context for CBC decryption.
AES (aes_small) key schedule context for CTR mode.
AES (aes_small) key schedule context for CTR + CBC-MAC.
AES (aes_ct) constant-time key schedule context for CBC encryption.
AES (aes_ct) constant-time key schedule context for CBC decryption.
AES (aes_ct) constant-time key schedule context for CTR mode.
AES (aes_ct) constant-time key schedule context for CTR + CBC-MAC.
AES (aes_ct64) 64-bit constant-time key schedule context for CBC encryption.
AES (aes_ct64) 64-bit constant-time key schedule context for CBC decryption.
AES (aes_ct64) 64-bit constant-time key schedule context for CTR mode.
AES (aes_ct64) 64-bit constant-time key schedule context for CTR + CBC-MAC.
AES (aes_x86ni) AES-NI key schedule context for CBC encryption; only on x86 with AES-NI.
AES (aes_x86ni) AES-NI key schedule context for CBC decryption.
AES (aes_x86ni) AES-NI key schedule context for CTR mode.
AES (aes_x86ni) AES-NI key schedule context for CTR + CBC-MAC.
AES (aes_pwr8) POWER8 crypto-opcodes key schedule context for CBC encryption.
AES (aes_pwr8) key schedule context for CBC decryption.
AES (aes_pwr8) key schedule context for CTR mode.
AES (aes_pwr8) key schedule context for CTR + CBC-MAC.
Union large enough to hold any AES CBC-encryption key context (any backend). Use when selecting implementation at runtime.
Union large enough to hold any AES CBC-decryption key context.
Union large enough to hold any AES CTR key context.
Union large enough to hold any AES CTR+CBC-MAC key context.
DES/3DES (des_tab) table-based key schedule context for CBC encryption.
DES/3DES (des_tab) table-based key schedule context for CBC decryption.
DES/3DES (des_ct) constant-time key schedule context for CBC encryption.
DES/3DES (des_ct) constant-time key schedule context for CBC decryption.
Union large enough to hold any DES/3DES CBC-encryption key context.
Union large enough to hold any DES/3DES CBC-decryption key context.

objects.definition:
typedef uint32_t (*br_chacha20_run)(const void *key,
	const void *iv, uint32_t cc, void *data, size_t len);
objects.description: Function pointer typedef for ChaCha20 stream cipher run function following RFC 7539. Returns updated 32-bit counter.
Function pointer typedef for AEAD ChaCha20+Poly1305 run function per RFC 7539. Performs encrypt/decrypt and tag computation.

Vtable (class) for hash function implementations. Holds context size, descriptor bitfield, and method pointers providing init/update/out/state/set_state. Constant instances (e.g., br_md5_vtable) implement specific hashes.
Opaque MD5 hash computation context. First field is the vtable pointer; remaining fields hold buffer, byte count, and chaining state. Movable and clonable; no explicit destruction needed.
Opaque SHA-1 hash computation context. Same OOP vtable model as other hashes. Movable/clonable.
Opaque SHA-224 context. Layout identical to SHA-256. Movable/clonable; no explicit release.
SHA-256 context type. In normal builds it is an alias of br_sha224_context and shares the same layout and functions for update/state/set_state via macros.
Opaque SHA-384 hash context. Layout identical to SHA-512. Uses 128-byte block buffer and 64-bit state words.
SHA-512 context type. In normal builds it is an alias of br_sha384_context and shares the same layout and functions for update/state/set_state via macros.
Context for the combined MD5+SHA-1 hash (concatenated outputs). Processes input once and maintains both MD5 and SHA-1 internal states.
Union large enough to hold any of the standard BearSSL hash contexts (including md5sha1). Useful for generic code selecting a hash at runtime.
Context for computing multiple standard hashes in parallel over the same input. Holds shared buffer, counters, per-hash state, and an array of implementation vtables. Not an OOP vtable-based context.

objects.definition: typedef void (*br_ghash)(void *y, const void *h, const void *data, size_t len);
objects.description: Function pointer type for GHASH implementations used by GCM. Updates a 16-byte y with key h over data (len bytes), zero-padding final block.

Opaque HMAC key context holding processed key material for a chosen hash (inner/outer pads) and a pointer to the hash vtable. Caller allocates it; no dynamic allocation or release function. Initialize with br_hmac_key_init(). Underlying hash must meet BearSSL HMAC constraints (state/output ≤ 64 bytes; block length power of two 16–256).

Opaque per-computation HMAC context that tracks hashing state, stored outer pad, and selected output length. Caller allocates it; no dynamic allocation or release function. Initialize from a br_hmac_key_context with br_hmac_init(), feed data with br_hmac_update(), finalize with br_hmac_out() or br_hmac_outCT().

Opaque HKDF context used to run HKDF-Extract and HKDF-Expand. It holds internal HMAC state, a buffer, and bookkeeping fields. Callers allocate it and use it via the br_hkdf_* API; there is no dynamic allocation and no explicit destroy function. Construction is via br_hkdf_init(), then inject data with br_hkdf_inject(), flip with br_hkdf_flip(), and produce bytes with br_hkdf_produce().

Opaque SHAKE (XOF) context supporting SHAKE128/SHAKE256 depending on chosen security level. It encapsulates the Keccak sponge state and buffering. Callers allocate it and use it via the br_shake_* API; there is no dynamic allocation and no explicit destroy function. Construct with br_shake_init(), absorb with br_shake_inject(), flip with br_shake_flip(), then squeeze with br_shake_produce().

Opaque PEM decoder context used with the BearSSL streamed PEM decoder. Holds internal state, stacks, and the destination callback for decoded data. No dynamic allocation; initialize with br_pem_decoder_init() and feed data via br_pem_decoder_push().
Seed chunk structure used by the TLS PRF functions to pass one segment of the concatenated PRF seed. Holds a pointer to bytes and their length; length may be zero and data may be NULL when len == 0.

Function pointer type for a TLS PRF implementation. Points to functions that expand a secret, label, and one or more seed chunks into an arbitrary-length output. Implementations matching this signature include br_tls10_prf, br_tls12_sha256_prf, and br_tls12_sha384_prf (declared here but not typedef aliases).

Vtable class describing a PRNG implementation. Instances (const vtables) expose function pointers for init, generate, and update and advertise required context size. Passed by pointer as the first field in PRNG contexts to support an OOP-style API.

Opaque context for the HMAC_DRBG PRNG. First field is a br_prng_class vtable pointer enabling the OOP API. Internals include K and V (per SP 800-90A) and a pointer to the hash vtable used for HMAC. Initialize with br_hmac_drbg_init, generate bytes with br_hmac_drbg_generate, and reseed with br_hmac_drbg_update.

Opaque context for the AESCTR_DRBG PRNG (custom AES-128-CTR–based generator). First field is a br_prng_class vtable pointer. Internal state includes AES CTR key schedule and a counter. Initialize with br_aesctr_drbg_init, generate with br_aesctr_drbg_generate, and update with br_aesctr_drbg_update.

objects.definition: typedef int (*br_prng_seeder)(const br_prng_class **ctx);
objects.description: Function pointer type for PRNG seeders that obtain entropy from a system or hardware source and inject it into a PRNG context. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: br_get_config
functions.description: Returns a read-only array of configuration options compiled into the BearSSL library. Each element is a br_config_option with a name (matching internal macro names) and a long value (booleans as 1/0; some numeric limits such as maximum key sizes expressed in bits). The array is terminated by an entry whose name is NULL. Typical usage: call once at startup or when reporting capabilities, iterate until name == NULL, and display or use the values.
requirements: The returned array is read-only; callers must not modify any element (const data).
The array is terminated by an entry with name == NULL; callers must stop iteration at this sentinel and must not access beyond it.
Do not free or deallocate the returned pointer or its contents; BearSSL does not use dynamic allocation and no release function is provided.
When iterating, check that name != NULL before dereferencing it to avoid reading past the sentinel.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_flags
functions.description: Return the current behavioural flags set on the SSL engine context.
requirements: cc must be a valid, initialised br_ssl_engine_context pointer.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_all_flags
functions.description: Overwrite all behavioural flags in the SSL engine with the given flags value.
requirements: cc must be valid.
Callers should understand the semantic of each BR_OPT_* flag before setting.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_add_flags
functions.description: Set (OR in) the specified behavioural flags without altering other flags.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_remove_flags
functions.description: Clear the specified behavioural flags without altering other flags.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_versions
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_versions(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, unsigned version_min, unsigned version_max)
functions.description: Set the minimum and maximum supported TLS versions for the engine.
requirements: version_min and version_max must be supported by the implementation (TLS 1.0, 1.1, 1.2).
version_max must be >= version_min.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_suites
functions.description: Configure the list of cipher suites to advertise/use. The array is copied into the engine.
requirements: suites must point to suites_num entries; array is copied at call time.
Suites provided must be supported by the engine; providing unsupported suites may cause negotiation failure.
No duplicates in the list.
For clients, TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV may be appended if voluntarily downgrading.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_x509
functions.description: Attach an already-initialised X.509 validation engine to the SSL engine.
requirements: x509ctx must refer to a properly initialised X.509 engine and remain valid while used.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_protocol_names
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_protocol_names(br_ssl_engine_context *ctx, const char **names, size_t num)
functions.description: Set supported ALPN protocol names for negotiation. Names are linked, not copied.
requirements: num must be >= 1.
Each name must be non-empty and <= 255 characters (excluding terminating NUL).
names array and pointed strings must remain valid for the lifetime of the connection.
ctx must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_selected_protocol
functions.description: Return the ALPN protocol selected during handshake, or NULL if none.
requirements: Must have previously set protocol names to get a non-NULL result.
Call valid anytime; returns one of the pointers previously provided.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_hash
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_hash(br_ssl_engine_context *ctx, int id, const br_hash_class *impl)
functions.description: Register or remove a hash implementation (MD5/SHA family) for TLS use by ID.
requirements: id must be a standard hash id (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224/256/384/512).
impl may be NULL to remove support for that id.
ctx must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_hash
functions.signature: static inline const br_hash_class * br_ssl_engine_get_hash(br_ssl_engine_context *ctx, int id)
functions.description: Retrieve the hash implementation previously set with br_ssl_engine_set_hash for the given id.
requirements: id must match a previously set hash id or returns NULL.
ctx must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_prf10
functions.description: Set or remove the PRF implementation for TLS 1.0/1.1.
requirements: impl may be NULL to remove.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_prf_sha256
functions.description: Set or remove the TLS 1.2 PRF implementation variant using SHA-256.
requirements: impl may be NULL to remove.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_prf_sha384
functions.description: Set or remove the TLS 1.2 PRF implementation variant using SHA-384.
requirements: impl may be NULL to remove.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_aes_cbc
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_aes_cbc(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, const br_block_cbcenc_class *impl_enc, const br_block_cbcdec_class *impl_dec)
functions.description: Set AES/CBC encryption and decryption implementations used by the engine.
requirements: Either impl may be NULL to disable that direction.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_aes_cbc
functions.description: Configure constant-time, platform-optimized AES/CBC implementations and record handlers in the engine.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_aes_ctr
functions.description: Set the AES/CTR implementation used by the engine (used e.g., for GCM).
requirements: impl may be NULL to disable.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_aes_gcm
functions.description: Configure platform-optimized AES/CTR and GHASH implementations and set GCM record handlers.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_des_cbc
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_des_cbc(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, const br_block_cbcenc_class *impl_enc, const br_block_cbcdec_class *impl_dec)
functions.description: Set DES/CBC encryption and decryption implementations used by the engine.
requirements: Either impl may be NULL to disable that direction.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_des_cbc
functions.description: Configure platform-optimized DES/CBC implementations and set CBC record handlers.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_ghash
functions.description: Set the GHASH implementation used for GCM mode.
requirements: impl may be NULL to disable.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_chacha20
functions.description: Set the ChaCha20 implementation used by the engine.
requirements: ichacha may be NULL to disable.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_poly1305
functions.description: Set the Poly1305 implementation used by the engine.
requirements: ipoly may be NULL to disable.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_chapol
functions.description: Configure platform-optimized ChaCha20 and Poly1305 implementations and set ChaCha20+Poly1305 record handlers.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_aes_ctrcbc
functions.description: Set the combined AES CTR+CBC implementation used by the engine (for CCM).
requirements: impl may be NULL to disable.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_aes_ccm
functions.description: Configure platform-optimized AES CTR+CBC implementation and set CCM record handlers.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_cbc
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_cbc(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, const br_sslrec_in_cbc_class *impl_in, const br_sslrec_out_cbc_class *impl_out)
functions.description: Set the record-layer engines for CBC+HMAC (inbound and outbound).
requirements: Either impl may be NULL to disable that direction.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_gcm
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_gcm(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, const br_sslrec_in_gcm_class *impl_in, const br_sslrec_out_gcm_class *impl_out)
functions.description: Set the record-layer engines for GCM (inbound and outbound).
requirements: Either impl may be NULL to disable that direction.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_ccm
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_ccm(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, const br_sslrec_in_ccm_class *impl_in, const br_sslrec_out_ccm_class *impl_out)
functions.description: Set the record-layer engines for CCM (inbound and outbound).
requirements: Either impl may be NULL to disable that direction.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_chapol
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_engine_set_chapol(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, const br_sslrec_in_chapol_class *impl_in, const br_sslrec_out_chapol_class *impl_out)
functions.description: Set the record-layer engines for ChaCha20+Poly1305 (inbound and outbound).
requirements: Either impl may be NULL to disable that direction.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_ec
functions.description: Set the elliptic curve implementation (used for ECDH/ECDHE/ECDSA).
requirements: iec may be NULL to disable EC-based suites.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_ec
functions.description: Configure the fastest available EC implementation on the current system.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_ec
functions.description: Get the EC implementation currently set in the engine.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_rsavrfy
functions.description: Set the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification implementation.
requirements: irsavrfy may be NULL to disable RSA signature verification.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_rsavrfy
functions.description: Configure the fastest available RSA signature verification implementation.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_rsavrfy
functions.description: Get the RSA signature verification implementation currently set.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_ecdsa
functions.description: Set the ECDSA signature verification implementation (uses configured EC core).
requirements: iecdsa may be NULL to disable ECDSA verification.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_default_ecdsa
functions.description: Configure the fastest available ECDSA verification and EC core implementations.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_ecdsa
functions.description: Get the ECDSA verification implementation currently set.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_buffer
functions.signature: void br_ssl_engine_set_buffer(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, void *iobuf, size_t iobuf_len, int bidi)
functions.description: Provide a single I/O buffer to the engine and choose half- or full-duplex operation. Buffer is linked (not copied).
requirements: After this call, you MUST call br_ssl_client_reset() or br_ssl_server_reset() before use.
iobuf must remain valid while the engine is used.
If bidi==0, half-duplex; optimal size BR_SSL_BUFSIZE_MONO; smaller sizes limit record support.
If bidi==1, full-duplex; optimal size BR_SSL_BUFSIZE_BIDI; smaller sizes bias input side.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_buffers_bidi
functions.signature: void br_ssl_engine_set_buffers_bidi(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, void *ibuf, size_t ibuf_len, void *obuf, size_t obuf_len)
functions.description: Provide separate input/output buffers for full-duplex operation. Buffers are linked (not copied).
requirements: After this call, you MUST call br_ssl_client_reset() or br_ssl_server_reset() before use.
ibuf/obuf must remain valid while the engine is used.
Optimal sizes are BR_SSL_BUFSIZE_INPUT and BR_SSL_BUFSIZE_OUTPUT; smaller sizes reduce capability.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_inject_entropy
functions.description: Inject additional entropy into the engine RNG. May be called multiple times; entropy is mixed cumulatively.
requirements: If OS entropy is unavailable, caller MUST inject enough entropy (>=80 bits, preferably >=128).
Quality of provided bytes is not assessed; caller must ensure unpredictability.
cc must be valid; data must point to len bytes if len>0.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_server_name
functions.signature: static inline const char * br_ssl_engine_get_server_name(const br_ssl_engine_context *cc)
functions.description: Return the SNI server name in the engine: client-provided (reset) or server-received (from ClientHello). Empty string if none.
requirements: cc must be valid. Returned pointer refers to internal buffer and may change during operation (e.g., renegotiation).

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_version
functions.description: Return the negotiated protocol version stored in current session parameters.
requirements: Meaningful after ServerHello (handshake progressed).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_session_parameters
functions.description: Copy current session parameters (including master secret) into caller-provided structure.
requirements: Should be called only after initial handshake completion (engine allows app data).
pp must point to writable br_ssl_session_parameters.
Handle resulting sensitive data securely.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_set_session_parameters
functions.description: Set session parameters (for client session resumption attempts) from caller-provided structure.
requirements: Use on client prior to a new handshake. No effect on server.
pp must point to a valid structure.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_get_ecdhe_curve
functions.description: Return the ECDHE curve identifier used for key exchange in the current/last handshake (indeterminate for non-ECDHE suites).
requirements: cc must be valid.
Value is set when ServerKeyExchange is sent/received for ECDHE suites.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_current_state
functions.description: Return current engine state flags (BR_SSL_CLOSED, BR_SSL_SENDREC, BR_SSL_RECVREC, BR_SSL_SENDAPP, BR_SSL_RECVAPP).
requirements: cc must be valid.
BR_SSL_CLOSED is exclusive; use br_ssl_engine_last_error() to distinguish normal close vs error.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_last_error
functions.description: Return sticky error indicator since last reset (BR_ERR_*), or 0 if OK.
requirements: Cleared only by br_ssl_client_reset() or br_ssl_server_reset().
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_sendapp_buf
functions.description: Get buffer to write outgoing application plaintext if engine can accept it; returns NULL if not ready.
requirements: If non-NULL is returned, caller may write up to *len bytes.
Does not modify engine state.
cc must be valid; len must be non-NULL.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_sendapp_ack
functions.description: Acknowledge that len bytes of application data were written into buffer from br_ssl_engine_sendapp_buf(). Triggers processing.
requirements: len must be > 0.
len must not exceed the value previously returned via br_ssl_engine_sendapp_buf().
Must be called only after a successful buffer query.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_recvapp_buf
functions.description: Get buffer containing received application data; returns NULL if none available.
requirements: If non-NULL is returned, caller may read up to *len bytes.
Does not modify engine state.
cc must be valid; len must be non-NULL.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_recvapp_ack
functions.description: Acknowledge that len bytes of received application data were consumed from buffer returned by br_ssl_engine_recvapp_buf().
requirements: len must be > 0.
len must not exceed the value previously returned via br_ssl_engine_recvapp_buf().
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_sendrec_buf
functions.description: Get buffer containing encrypted record bytes ready to send; returns NULL if none.
requirements: If non-NULL is returned, caller may read up to *len bytes to send to transport.
Does not modify engine state.
cc must be valid; len must be non-NULL.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_sendrec_ack
functions.description: Acknowledge that len bytes were sent from the buffer returned by br_ssl_engine_sendrec_buf().
requirements: len must be > 0.
len must not exceed the value previously returned via br_ssl_engine_sendrec_buf().
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_recvrec_buf
functions.description: Get buffer where incoming record bytes should be written; returns NULL if engine not ready to receive records.
requirements: If non-NULL is returned, caller may write up to *len bytes into the buffer from transport.
Does not modify engine state.
cc must be valid; len must be non-NULL.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_recvrec_ack
functions.description: Inform engine that len bytes of incoming record data were written into buffer returned by br_ssl_engine_recvrec_buf().
requirements: len must be > 0.
len must not exceed the value previously returned via br_ssl_engine_recvrec_buf().
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_flush
functions.description: Wrap any buffered application data into a record and mark for sending. If no app data and force!=0, may send an empty record (keep-alive).
requirements: Some peer stacks may not accept empty records; use force with care.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_close
functions.description: Initiate TLS closure by assembling a close_notify alert if the context is open and ready, and mark it for sending.
requirements: Only assembles alert if context is open and ready.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_engine_renegotiate
functions.description: Request a secure renegotiation. Returns 1 if a renegotiation was triggered (or already ongoing), 0 otherwise.
requirements: Returns 0 if engine is failed/closed, peer lacks secure renegotiation support, BR_OPT_NO_RENEGOTIATION is set, or incoming app data buffered.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_key_export
functions.signature: int br_ssl_key_export(br_ssl_engine_context *cc, void *dst, size_t len, const char *label, const void *context, size_t context_len)
functions.description: Export RFC 5705 keying material of arbitrary length from a connected SSL engine into dst.
requirements: Engine must be in application data state (initial handshake finished, not failed/closed), else returns 0.
If context!=NULL, context_len must be <= 65535; context may be non-NULL with context_len==0 to request 'with context' variant.
dst must have at least len bytes writable.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_get_server_hashes
functions.description: Return bitfield of hash functions/signature algorithms the server supports for client authentication.
requirements: Call after server capabilities have been parsed (during/after CertificateRequest).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_get_server_curve
functions.description: Return curve ID of the server's public key (0 if not EC).
requirements: Set during certificate processing.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_init_full
functions.signature: void br_ssl_client_init_full(br_ssl_client_context *cc, br_x509_minimal_context *xc, const br_x509_trust_anchor *trust_anchors, size_t trust_anchors_num)
functions.description: Initialise client context with all supported algorithms/suites and initialise a minimal X.509 validator with given trust anchors.
requirements: cc and xc must be valid pointers.
trust_anchors must point to trust_anchors_num entries (copied/linked per implementation; header says X.509 engine is initialised here).

functions.name: br_ssl_client_zero
functions.description: Clear a client context completely (buffer references, implementations, cipher suites, state). Use to build a custom profile.
requirements: cc must be valid.
Context must be reconfigured after this before use.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_set_client_certificate
functions.description: Attach an external client-certificate handler (policy) context to the client for client auth.
requirements: pctx must point to the handler's vtable field and remain valid.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_set_rsapub
functions.description: Set RSA public-key encryption implementation used for encrypting the premaster secret in RSA key exchange suites.
requirements: irsapub may be NULL to disable RSA key exchange.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_set_default_rsapub
functions.description: Configure the fastest available RSA public-key operation implementation for the client.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_set_min_clienthello_len
functions.description: Set a minimum ClientHello length; if shorter, RFC 7685 padding extension is added to reach at least len bytes (excluding 4-byte handshake header).
requirements: Effect is on ClientHello construction; len is target size of ClientHello contents (without handshake header).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_reset
functions.signature: int br_ssl_client_reset(br_ssl_client_context *cc, const char *server_name, int resume_session)
functions.description: Prepare/reset client context for a new connection, optionally with SNI server_name and session resumption.
requirements: Must have set I/O buffers prior to use.
server_name may be NULL to send no SNI and skip name checking in minimal X.509 engine.
If resume_session!=0, previous session params may be reused if present/accepted; can also be set explicitly via br_ssl_engine_set_session_parameters().
Returns 0 on failure (e.g., no entropy injected nor obtainable).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_forget_session
functions.description: Forget any stored session so the next handshake will be a full handshake.
requirements: cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_set_single_rsa
functions.signature: void br_ssl_client_set_single_rsa(br_ssl_client_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_rsa_private_key *sk, br_rsa_pkcs1_sign irsasign)
functions.description: Configure a single-chain RSA client certificate and private key for client authentication. Trust anchor DN from server are ignored.
requirements: chain points to chain_len certificates in SSL order (EE first).
sk must be a valid RSA private key; irsasign must be provided for signatures.
The chain and key are linked in; they must remain valid for the connection duration (including renegotiations).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_client_set_single_ec
functions.signature: void br_ssl_client_set_single_ec(br_ssl_client_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_ec_private_key *sk, unsigned allowed_usages, unsigned cert_issuer_key_type, const br_ec_impl *iec, br_ecdsa_sign iecdsa)
functions.description: Configure a single-chain EC client certificate and EC private key. May allow static ECDH and/or ECDSA signatures.
requirements: chain points to chain_len certificates (EE first).
sk must be a valid EC private key.
allowed_usages is a bitmask of BR_KEYTYPE_KEYX and/or BR_KEYTYPE_SIGN.
cert_issuer_key_type must be BR_KEYTYPE_RSA or BR_KEYTYPE_EC (used for full static ECDH; ignored in TLS 1.2).
If ECDSA signatures are used, iecdsa must be provided; otherwise iecdsa may be 0.
iec is the EC core implementation to use.
Chain and key are linked in and must remain valid for the connection (including renegotiations).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_get_client_suites
functions.signature: static inline const br_suite_translated * br_ssl_server_get_client_suites(const br_ssl_server_context *cc, size_t *num)
functions.description: Return the list of translated cipher suites supported by both client and server, in preference order.
requirements: Call only after ClientHello has been processed (typically from policy).
Returned pointer refers to context-owned array rewritten on each handshake.
cc and num must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_get_client_hashes
functions.description: Return bitfield of hash functions/signature algorithms supported by the client.
requirements: Meaningful after ClientHello processing.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_get_client_curves
functions.description: Return bitfield of named elliptic curves supported by the client.
requirements: Meaningful after ClientHello processing.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_zero
functions.description: Clear a server context completely (buffer references, implementations, cipher suites, state). Use to build a custom profile.
requirements: cc must be valid.
Context must be reconfigured before reuse.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_set_policy
functions.description: Attach an external server policy context (handler) for suite selection and private-key operations.
requirements: pctx must point to the handler's vtable field and remain valid.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_set_single_rsa
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_set_single_rsa(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_rsa_private_key *sk, unsigned allowed_usages, br_rsa_private irsacore, br_rsa_pkcs1_sign irsasign)
functions.description: Use built-in policy context to configure a single RSA certificate chain and private key for server. Enables suites per allowed_usages.
requirements: chain points to chain_len certificates to send to the client.
sk is the RSA private key.
allowed_usages is combination of BR_KEYTYPE_KEYX and/or BR_KEYTYPE_SIGN.
irsacore and irsasign implementations must be provided.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_set_single_ec
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_set_single_ec(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_ec_private_key *sk, unsigned allowed_usages, unsigned cert_issuer_key_type, const br_ec_impl *iec, br_ecdsa_sign iecdsa)
functions.description: Use built-in policy context to configure a single EC certificate chain and EC private key for server. Enables suites per allowed_usages, supports ECDH/ECDHE.
requirements: chain points to chain_len certificates to send to the client.
sk is the EC private key.
allowed_usages is combination of BR_KEYTYPE_KEYX and/or BR_KEYTYPE_SIGN.
cert_issuer_key_type is BR_KEYTYPE_RSA or BR_KEYTYPE_EC (needed to support TLS_ECDH_* suites).
iec and iecdsa implementations must be provided (iecdsa for signatures).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_set_trust_anchor_names
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_server_set_trust_anchor_names(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x500_name *ta_names, size_t num)
functions.description: Enable client certificate authentication by supplying encoded trust anchor DNs to send to client (linked, not copied).
requirements: If num==0, client auth is disabled.
ta_names must remain valid as long as used.
Mutually exclusive with setting tas via alt variant (engine uses either names or tas).
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_set_trust_anchor_names_alt
functions.signature: static inline void br_ssl_server_set_trust_anchor_names_alt(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_trust_anchor *tas, size_t num)
functions.description: Enable client certificate authentication by supplying trust anchors (only dn fields used). Linked, not copied.
requirements: tas must remain valid as long as used.
Mutually exclusive with ta_names variant (engine uses either names or tas).
If num==0, client auth is disabled.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_set_cache
functions.description: Attach a session parameter cache (via its vtable) to the server.
requirements: vtable must point to a valid cache context and remain valid.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_reset
functions.description: Prepare/reset server context for handling a new incoming client connection.
requirements: Must have set I/O buffer(s) prior to use.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_full_rsa
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_full_rsa(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_rsa_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with all supported algorithms/suites for RSA server keys.
requirements: cc must be valid.
chain points to chain_len certificates; sk must be valid RSA private key.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_full_ec
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_full_ec(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, unsigned cert_issuer_key_type, const br_ec_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with all supported algorithms/suites for EC server keys; requires CA key type to support TLS_ECDH_* suites.
requirements: cert_issuer_key_type must be BR_KEYTYPE_RSA or BR_KEYTYPE_EC.
cc, chain, sk must be valid; chain_len correct.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_minr2g
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_minr2g(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_rsa_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with minimal profile using TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (no forward secrecy).
requirements: RSA server key and matching chain required.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_mine2g
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_mine2g(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_rsa_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with minimal profile using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (forward secrecy).
requirements: RSA server key and chain required.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_minf2g
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_minf2g(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_ec_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with minimal profile using TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (forward secrecy).
requirements: EC server key and chain required.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_minu2g
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_minu2g(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_ec_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with minimal profile using TLS_ECDH_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (no forward secrecy; CA used RSA).
requirements: EC server key and chain required.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_minv2g
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_minv2g(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_ec_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with minimal profile using TLS_ECDH_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (no forward secrecy; CA used EC).
requirements: EC server key and chain required.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_mine2c
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_mine2c(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_rsa_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with minimal profile using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 (forward secrecy).
requirements: RSA server key and chain required.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_server_init_minf2c
functions.signature: void br_ssl_server_init_minf2c(br_ssl_server_context *cc, const br_x509_certificate *chain, size_t chain_len, const br_ec_private_key *sk)
functions.description: Initialise server with minimal profile using TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 (forward secrecy).
requirements: EC server key and chain required.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_session_cache_lru_init
functions.description: Initialise an LRU session cache using provided storage (each entry 100 bytes). Maintains a search tree and LRU list.
requirements: store must point to store_len bytes and remain valid for cache lifetime.
store_len can be any size up to 2^32-1; capacity is store_len/100 entries.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_ssl_session_cache_lru_forget
functions.description: Forget/disable an entry with the given 32-byte session ID, if present.
requirements: id must point to exactly 32 bytes.
cc must have been initialised.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_sslio_init
functions.signature: void br_sslio_init(br_sslio_context *ctx, br_ssl_engine_context *engine, int (*low_read)(void *read_context, unsigned char *data, size_t len), void *read_context, int (*low_write)(void *write_context, const unsigned char *data, size_t len), void *write_context)
functions.description: Initialise simplified I/O wrapper around an SSL engine using user-provided transport callbacks (low_read/low_write).
requirements: engine must be a valid, initialised SSL engine.
low_read must read 1..len bytes into data and return count, or -1 on error. Should block until at least one byte; returning 0 is tolerated but leads to immediate retry.
low_write must write 1..len bytes from data and return count, or -1 on error. Should block similarly; 0 tolerated but leads to retry.
len passed to callbacks is never 0 and <20000.
Errors (-1) are permanent and terminate SSL.
ctx must be valid.

functions.name: br_sslio_read
functions.description: Read up to len bytes of application data via the SSL wrapper. Returns number of bytes (never 0 unless len==0), or -1 on error/closure.
requirements: If len==0, returns 0 immediately; otherwise, will only return after reading at least one byte or an error (-1).
Caller should check engine error to distinguish normal closure vs error.
cc and dst must be valid.

functions.name: br_sslio_read_all
functions.description: Read exactly len bytes of application data unless an error/closure occurs. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: Treat a verified normal SSL closure before receiving len bytes as error (-1).
cc and dst must be valid.

functions.name: br_sslio_write
functions.signature: int br_sslio_write(br_sslio_context *cc, const void *src, size_t len)
functions.description: Write up to len bytes of application data via the SSL wrapper. Returns number of bytes written (never 0 unless len==0), or -1 on error/closure. Writing injects into SSL buffers.
requirements: If len==0, returns 0 immediately; otherwise, returns after writing at least one byte or error.
Use br_sslio_flush() to ensure pending data is sent to transport.
cc and src must be valid.

functions.name: br_sslio_write_all
functions.signature: int br_sslio_write_all(br_sslio_context *cc, const void *src, size_t len)
functions.description: Write exactly len bytes of application data unless an error/closure occurs. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Writing injects into SSL buffers.
requirements: Use br_sslio_flush() to ensure pending data is sent to transport.
Treat a verified normal SSL closure before writing len bytes as error (-1).
cc and src must be valid.

functions.name: br_sslio_flush
functions.description: Ensure all buffered application data in the wrapper and SSL engine has been sent to the transport (accepted by low_write). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: If there is no pending data, does nothing and returns success.
cc must be valid.

functions.name: br_sslio_close
functions.description: Perform SSL closure protocol (send close_notify and wait for peer close_notify). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (including peer not completing closure).
requirements: cc must be valid.
On return the SSL connection is finished; caller should handle transport termination if applicable.

functions.name: br_x509_knownkey_init_rsa
functions.description: Initialize a "known key" X.509 engine with a known RSA public key. The engine ignores any presented certificates and always returns the configured key with the specified allowed usages. Pointers are linked, not copied, so the key memory must outlive the engine’s use.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable br_x509_knownkey_context.
pk must point to a valid RSA public key structure whose memory remains valid for as long as the key may be used by the engine.
usages must be a combination of BR_KEYTYPE_KEYX and/or BR_KEYTYPE_SIGN.

functions.name: br_x509_knownkey_init_ec
functions.description: Initialize a "known key" X.509 engine with a known EC public key. The engine ignores any presented certificates and always returns the configured key with the specified allowed usages. Pointers are linked, not copied.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable br_x509_knownkey_context.
pk must point to a valid EC public key structure whose memory remains valid for as long as the key may be used by the engine.
usages must be a combination of BR_KEYTYPE_KEYX and/or BR_KEYTYPE_SIGN.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_init
functions.signature: void br_x509_minimal_init(br_x509_minimal_context *ctx, const br_hash_class *dn_hash_impl, const br_x509_trust_anchor *trust_anchors, size_t trust_anchors_num);
functions.description: Initialize the "minimal" X.509 engine. Sets up the context, chooses the hash used internally for DN comparisons, and registers the trust anchor array. After this call, you must configure signature verification implementations (hashes and RSA/ECDSA) before validating chains.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable br_x509_minimal_context.
dn_hash_impl should be a valid hash implementation; a collision‑resistant hash is advised.
trust_anchors must point to an array of br_x509_trust_anchor of length trust_anchors_num; the array must remain valid for the lifetime of the context usage.

After initialization, the caller MUST set hash and signature verification implementations (e.g., via br_x509_minimal_set_hash, br_x509_minimal_set_rsa, br_x509_minimal_set_ecdsa) before using the engine for validation.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_set_hash
functions.signature: static inline void br_x509_minimal_set_hash(br_x509_minimal_context *ctx, int id, const br_hash_class *impl);
functions.description: Enable or disable support for a specific hash function in the minimal X.509 engine. Supported ids are the standard BearSSL ids 1..6 (MD5, SHA‑1, SHA‑224, SHA‑256, SHA‑384, SHA‑512). Passing NULL removes support for that hash.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_minimal_context.
id must be one of 1..6.
impl may be NULL to disable that hash id; otherwise it must be a valid hash implementation compatible with BearSSL.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_set_rsa
functions.description: Set or disable the RSA (PKCS#1 v1.5) signature verification implementation used by the minimal engine. Pass 0 to disable RSA support.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_minimal_context.
irsa may be 0 to disable RSA; otherwise it must be a valid function pointer of type br_rsa_pkcs1_vrfy.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_set_ecdsa
functions.signature: static inline void br_x509_minimal_set_ecdsa(br_x509_minimal_context *ctx, const br_ec_impl *iec, br_ecdsa_vrfy iecdsa);
functions.description: Set or disable the ECDSA signature verification implementation (ASN.1 format) for the minimal engine, along with the elliptic curve implementation it uses. Pass 0 for iecdsa to disable ECDSA support.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_minimal_context.
If iecdsa is 0, ECDSA support is disabled and iec may be NULL.
If iecdsa is non‑zero, it must be a valid ECDSA verification function (format "asn1"), and iec should be a valid elliptic curve implementation used by that verifier.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_init_full
functions.description: Initialize the minimal engine like br_x509_minimal_init(), and also set default implementations for RSA, ECDSA, and the standard hash functions. Useful for quickly preparing a working validator with provided trust anchors.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable br_x509_minimal_context.
trust_anchors must point to an array of br_x509_trust_anchor of length trust_anchors_num; the array must remain valid while the context is used.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_set_time
functions.signature: static inline void br_x509_minimal_set_time(br_x509_minimal_context *ctx, uint32_t days, uint32_t seconds);
functions.description: Set a fixed validation time (UTC) for the minimal engine, as days since 0000‑01‑01 and seconds since midnight. Overrides any time callback. If not set and no system time is available, validation may fail (except direct trust).
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_minimal_context.
seconds must be in the range 0..86400.
days is an absolute day count in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_set_time_callback
functions.signature: static inline void br_x509_minimal_set_time_callback(br_x509_minimal_context *ctx, void *itime_ctx, br_x509_time_check itime);
functions.description: Provide a callback to check each certificate’s validity range against the current time. The callback is invoked for each certificate during path validation with the provided context pointer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_minimal_context.

itime may be NULL to clear the callback; otherwise it must follow the br_x509_time_check contract: return -1 if before notBefore, +1 if after notAfter, 0 if within, any other value to signal time unavailable.
itime_ctx is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback.

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_set_minrsa
functions.description: Set the minimal acceptable RSA key length (in bytes) for keys extracted from certificates (EE and intermediates) in the minimal engine. Shorter keys cause validation failure. Default minimum is 128 bytes (~1017 bits).
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_minimal_context.
byte_length is the minimum modulus length in bytes; it is applied to certificate keys (not to CA trust anchors).

functions.name: br_x509_minimal_set_name_elements
functions.signature: static inline void br_x509_minimal_set_name_elements(br_x509_minimal_context *ctx, br_name_element *elts, size_t num_elts);
functions.description: Configure which name elements to extract from the end‑entity certificate’s subject DN or SAN during validation. The array is linked into the context and filled in encounter order.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_minimal_context.
elts may be NULL only if num_elts is 0; otherwise it must point to an array of num_elts br_name_element structures that remain valid during decoding.
Each br_name_element.buf must be at least 1 byte long (len >= 1).

functions.name: br_x509_decoder_init
functions.signature: void br_x509_decoder_init(br_x509_decoder_context *ctx, void (*append_dn)(void *ctx, const void *buf, size_t len), void *append_dn_ctx);
functions.description: Initialize an X.509 certificate decoder context for extracting names and public keys (not for full validation). Optionally provide a callback to receive the subject DN bytes as they are decoded.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable br_x509_decoder_context.
append_dn may be NULL to ignore the subject DN; otherwise it must accept incremental chunks and can be called multiple times.
append_dn_ctx is an opaque pointer passed to append_dn.

functions.name: br_x509_decoder_push
functions.description: Feed a chunk of DER certificate bytes to the decoder. Call repeatedly until the whole certificate has been provided.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_decoder_context previously initialized with br_x509_decoder_init().
If len is non‑zero, data must point to at least len valid bytes.
Provide the complete certificate content for successful decoding.

functions.name: br_x509_decoder_get_pkey
functions.description: Return a pointer to the decoded public key after successful decoding, or NULL if decoding has not finished or failed. The returned pointer refers to memory inside the decoder context and becomes invalid if the context is reused or released.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_decoder_context.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
Do not reuse or free the context before copying/using the key if you need it after context reuse.

functions.name: br_x509_decoder_last_error
functions.description: Get the current/last decoding status. Returns 0 if decoding succeeded; BR_ERR_X509_TRUNCATED if decoding is not yet finished; otherwise a non‑zero BR_ERR_X509_* error code.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_decoder_context.

functions.name: br_x509_decoder_isCA
functions.description: Return the Basic Constraints CA flag from the successfully decoded certificate. Indicates whether the certificate asserts CA=true.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_decoder_context.
Only read this after successful decoding (i.e., br_x509_decoder_last_error() returned 0).

functions.name: br_x509_decoder_get_signer_key_type
functions.description: Return the issuer’s key type (algorithm used to sign the decoded certificate): BR_KEYTYPE_RSA or BR_KEYTYPE_EC, or 0 if unrecognized.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_decoder_context.
Value is meaningful only after successful decoding.

functions.name: br_x509_decoder_get_signer_hash_id
functions.description: Return the identifier of the hash function used in the certificate’s signature, or 0 if unrecognized.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_x509_decoder_context.
Value is meaningful only after successful decoding.

functions.name: br_skey_decoder_init
functions.description: Initialize a private key decoder context capable of decoding RSA or EC private keys in raw DER or unencrypted PKCS#8 formats.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable br_skey_decoder_context.

functions.name: br_skey_decoder_push
functions.description: Feed a chunk of private key data (raw DER or unencrypted PKCS#8) to the decoder. Call repeatedly until the full key has been provided.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_skey_decoder_context previously initialized with br_skey_decoder_init().
If len is non‑zero, data must point to at least len valid bytes.
Provide the complete key content for successful decoding.

functions.name: br_skey_decoder_last_error
functions.description: Return the decoder status for the private key: 0 on success; BR_ERR_X509_TRUNCATED if decoding is unfinished; or a non‑zero error code on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_skey_decoder_context.

functions.name: br_skey_decoder_key_type
functions.description: Return the decoded private key type (BR_KEYTYPE_RSA or BR_KEYTYPE_EC), or 0 if decoding is unfinished or failed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_skey_decoder_context.
Meaningful only after successful decoding.

functions.name: br_skey_decoder_get_rsa
functions.description: Return a pointer to the decoded RSA private key, or NULL if decoding failed/unfinished or the key is not RSA. The returned structures are owned by the context and become invalid if the context is reused or released.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_skey_decoder_context.
Caller must check for NULL before use.
Do not reuse or free the context before copying/using the key if you need it after context reuse.

functions.name: br_skey_decoder_get_ec
functions.description: Return a pointer to the decoded EC private key, or NULL if decoding failed/unfinished or the key is not EC. The returned structures are owned by the context and become invalid if the context is reused or released.
requirements: ctx must be a valid br_skey_decoder_context.
Caller must check for NULL before use.
Do not reuse or free the context before copying/using the key if you need it after context reuse.

functions.name: br_encode_rsa_raw_der
functions.signature: size_t br_encode_rsa_raw_der(void *dest, const br_rsa_private_key *sk, const br_rsa_public_key *pk, const void *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Encode an RSA private key into PKCS#1 RSAPrivateKey (DER). If dest is NULL, returns the required size without writing. Public key elements (n,e) and private exponent d are taken from parameters; they can be recomputed from sk if needed by the caller.
requirements: sk must point to a valid RSA private key (p, q, dp, dq, iq populated).
pk must point to a valid RSA public key (n, e populated).
d must point to the private exponent bytes, with length dlen, consistent with the key.
dest may be NULL to query the length; otherwise it must point to a buffer large enough to hold the encoded key.

functions.name: br_encode_rsa_pkcs8_der
functions.signature: size_t br_encode_rsa_pkcs8_der(void *dest, const br_rsa_private_key *sk, const br_rsa_public_key *pk, const void *d, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Encode an RSA private key into PKCS#8 OneAsymmetricKey (DER), wrapping the PKCS#1 RSAPrivateKey produced by br_encode_rsa_raw_der(). If dest is NULL, returns the required size without writing.
requirements: sk must point to a valid RSA private key (p, q, dp, dq, iq populated).
pk must point to a valid RSA public key (n, e populated).
d must point to the private exponent bytes, length dlen.
dest may be NULL to query the length; otherwise it must point to a buffer large enough to hold the encoded PKCS#8.

functions.name: br_encode_ec_raw_der
functions.signature: size_t br_encode_ec_raw_der(void *dest, const br_ec_private_key *sk, const br_ec_public_key *pk);
functions.description: Encode an EC private key into RFC 5915 ECPrivateKey (DER). If pk is provided, the publicKey field is included; otherwise it is omitted. Returns 0 if the key cannot be encoded (e.g., unknown OID for the curve). If dest is NULL, returns required size without writing.
requirements: sk must point to a valid EC private key (including correct curve identifier).
pk may be NULL; if non‑NULL, it must be a valid EC public key corresponding to sk.
dest may be NULL to query the length; otherwise it must point to a buffer large enough for the encoded key.
Encoding will fail (return 0) if there is no known OBJECT IDENTIFIER for the key’s curve.

functions.name: br_encode_ec_pkcs8_der
functions.signature: size_t br_encode_ec_pkcs8_der(void *dest, const br_ec_private_key *sk, const br_ec_public_key *pk);
functions.description: Encode an EC private key into PKCS#8 OneAsymmetricKey (DER). The privateKey content is the DER of ECPrivateKey (RFC 5915) without the parameters field; the curve is identified via OID in the privateKeyAlgorithm. If pk is non‑NULL, the public key is included in ECPrivateKey’s publicKey field. Returns 0 on inability to encode (e.g., unknown curve OID). If dest is NULL, returns required size without writing.
requirements: sk must point to a valid EC private key with a curve that has a known OBJECT IDENTIFIER.
pk may be NULL; if non‑NULL, it must be a valid EC public key corresponding to sk.
dest may be NULL to query the length; otherwise it must point to a buffer large enough for the encoded key.
Function returns 0 if the curve OID is unknown (cannot encode).

functions.name: br_ec_p256_m62_get
functions.description: Return a pointer to the specialised P-256 EC implementation that relies on 64x64->128-bit multiplication ("m62"), if available on the current platform; otherwise return NULL (0). Use this to select a faster P-256 implementation when supported.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL before using the implementation.

functions.name: br_ec_p256_m64_get
functions.description: Return a pointer to the specialised P-256 EC implementation that relies on 64x64->128-bit multiplication ("m64"), if available on the current platform; otherwise return NULL (0).
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL before using the implementation.

functions.name: br_ec_c25519_m62_get
functions.description: Return a pointer to the specialised Curve25519 EC implementation that relies on 64x64->128-bit multiplication ("m62"), if available on the current platform; otherwise return NULL (0).
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL before using the implementation.

functions.name: br_ec_c25519_m64_get
functions.description: Return a pointer to the specialised Curve25519 EC implementation that relies on 64x64->128-bit multiplication ("m64"), if available on the current platform; otherwise return NULL (0).
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL before using the implementation.

functions.name: br_ec_get_default
functions.description: Return a pointer to the preferred/default EC implementation for the current system. Use this when you want BearSSL to choose the best available EC backend.
requirements: None beyond passing no arguments; the returned pointer should be treated as read-only.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_raw_to_asn1
functions.description: Convert an ECDSA signature from raw format (r||s, big-endian) to ASN.1 DER SEQUENCE format in place. Returns the new signature length on success, or 0 on error (e.g., odd raw length or oversized integer). May enlarge the signature by up to 9 bytes.
requirements: sig must point to a writable buffer that contains the raw signature and has enough capacity to accommodate up to sig_len + 9 bytes.
sig may be NULL only if sig_len is 0; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to mutable memory.
The raw signature length must be even (concatenation of r and s of equal length).
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates conversion failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_asn1_to_raw
functions.description: Convert an ECDSA signature from ASN.1 DER SEQUENCE format to raw format (r||s, big-endian) in place. Returns the new raw length on success, or 0 on error (e.g., invalid ASN.1 or oversized integer). The resulting raw length will be less than twice the source ASN.1 length at most.
requirements: sig must point to a writable buffer containing the ASN.1 signature and have enough capacity for the in-place expansion (worst-case strictly less than 2 * sig_len bytes).
Caller must provide a valid DER-encoded ECDSA signature; otherwise the function returns 0.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates conversion failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i31_sign_asn1
functions.signature: size_t br_ecdsa_i31_sign_asn1(const br_ec_impl *impl, const br_hash_class *hf, const void *hash_value, const br_ec_private_key *sk, void *sig);
functions.description: Generate an ECDSA signature (ASN.1/DER format) using the "i31" big-integer EC implementation. The hash length is inferred from the provided hash function class. Returns the signature length on success, or 0 on error (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must point to an EC implementation that supports sk->curve.
hf must point to a valid hash function class consistent with the size of hash_value.
hash_value must point to the hash output computed over the message with hf.
sk must reference a properly initialized EC private key for the targeted curve.
sig must point to a writable buffer large enough for the ASN.1 signature (up to 72 bytes for P-256, 104 for P-384, 139 for P-521 as documented).
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i31_sign_raw
functions.signature: size_t br_ecdsa_i31_sign_raw(const br_ec_impl *impl, const br_hash_class *hf, const void *hash_value, const br_ec_private_key *sk, void *sig);
functions.description: Generate an ECDSA signature (raw format r||s) using the "i31" EC implementation. Hash length is inferred from hf. Returns the signature length on success, or 0 on error (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must support sk->curve.
hf must describe the hash used to produce hash_value; its output size determines processing.
hash_value must point to the computed hash of the message.
sk must be a valid EC private key for the curve.
sig must point to a writable buffer large enough for the raw signature (64 bytes for P-256, 96 for P-384, 132 for P-521).
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i31_vrfy_asn1
functions.signature: uint32_t br_ecdsa_i31_vrfy_asn1(const br_ec_impl *impl, const void *hash, size_t hash_len, const br_ec_public_key *pk, const void *sig, size_t sig_len);
functions.description: Verify an ECDSA signature in ASN.1/DER format using the "i31" EC implementation. Returns 1 if the signature is valid, 0 otherwise (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must support pk->curve.
hash must point to the hash of the message; hash_len must match the actual hash length provided.
pk must reference a valid EC public key for the curve.
sig must point to the ASN.1-encoded ECDSA signature; sig_len is its length.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates verification failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i31_vrfy_raw
functions.signature: uint32_t br_ecdsa_i31_vrfy_raw(const br_ec_impl *impl, const void *hash, size_t hash_len, const br_ec_public_key *pk, const void *sig, size_t sig_len);
functions.description: Verify an ECDSA signature in raw (r||s) format using the "i31" EC implementation. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must support pk->curve.
hash must point to the message hash; hash_len must specify its byte length.
pk must be a valid EC public key for the curve.
sig must point to the raw signature of length matching r||s concatenation; sig_len is its length.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates verification failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i15_sign_asn1
functions.signature: size_t br_ecdsa_i15_sign_asn1(const br_ec_impl *impl, const br_hash_class *hf, const void *hash_value, const br_ec_private_key *sk, void *sig);
functions.description: Generate an ECDSA signature (ASN.1/DER format) using the "i15" big-integer EC implementation. Hash length is inferred from hf. Returns the signature length on success, or 0 on error (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must support sk->curve.
hf must be a valid hash function class; its output size matches hash_value.
hash_value must contain the hash of the message.
sk must be a properly initialized EC private key for the curve.
sig must be large enough for the ASN.1 signature (up to 72/104/139 bytes for P-256/P-384/P-521).
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i15_sign_raw
functions.signature: size_t br_ecdsa_i15_sign_raw(const br_ec_impl *impl, const br_hash_class *hf, const void *hash_value, const br_ec_private_key *sk, void *sig);
functions.description: Generate an ECDSA signature (raw r||s format) using the "i15" EC implementation. Returns the signature length on success, or 0 on error (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must support sk->curve.
hf must correspond to the hash used to produce hash_value.
hash_value must point to the message hash.
sk must be a valid EC private key for the curve.
sig must be large enough for the raw signature (64/96/132 bytes for P-256/P-384/P-521).
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i15_vrfy_asn1
functions.signature: uint32_t br_ecdsa_i15_vrfy_asn1(const br_ec_impl *impl, const void *hash, size_t hash_len, const br_ec_public_key *pk, const void *sig, size_t sig_len);
functions.description: Verify an ECDSA signature in ASN.1/DER format using the "i15" EC implementation. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must support pk->curve.
hash must point to the message hash, and hash_len must match its size.
pk must be a valid EC public key for the curve.
sig must point to the ASN.1-encoded signature; sig_len is its length.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates verification failure.

functions.name: br_ecdsa_i15_vrfy_raw
functions.signature: uint32_t br_ecdsa_i15_vrfy_raw(const br_ec_impl *impl, const void *hash, size_t hash_len, const br_ec_public_key *pk, const void *sig, size_t sig_len);
functions.description: Verify an ECDSA signature in raw (r||s) format using the "i15" EC implementation. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error (including when the key’s curve is not supported by impl).
requirements: impl must support pk->curve.
